text:
{
  "background_info": "Student Name: Rahul Verma
Age / Grade: 14 years / Grade 9
School: Navodaya Vidyalaya, Pune
Date of IEP Meeting: 19 October 2026
Disability Classification: Visual Impairment (moderate) under the RPwD Act 2016
Dominant Language: English and Hindi
Date Services Begin: 2 November 2026
Date Services Continue Through: 31 March 2027
Parent/Guardian: Mr. and Mrs. Verma (Contact details maintained in school records)
Medical Alerts: Moderate visual impairment resulting in rapid ocular fatigue and reduced visual efficiency with standard 10-12 point font; requires adapted lighting, enlarged materials, and regular visual breaks; no other medical conditions.",
  "academic_performance": "Present Level: Academic/Educational Achievement - Rahul Verma is currently functioning at grade level in core academic subjects, demonstrating exceptional proficiency and motivation in Mathematics and Science, having maintained a 78% academic record in Grade 8 with minimal support. Visual fatigue caused by small, dense print impacts his sustained reading speed in text-heavy subjects, though his underlying cognitive comprehension remains strong when materials are enlarged.

Present Level: Cognitive Ability - Rahul Verma is currently functioning at grade level in intellectual and cognitive processing, exhibiting strong logical reasoning, conceptual grasp, and problem-solving abilities across abstract subjects.

Present Level: Language Ability - Rahul Verma is currently functioning at grade level in receptive and expressive language skills, displaying articulate oral communication, active classroom verbal participation, and advanced auditory listening comprehension in both English and Hindi.

Present Level: Learning Style - Rahul Verma is currently functioning at grade level using an auditory and low-vision learning profile, relying on verbal instructions, auditory resources, large-print (18-24 point font) reading matter, and digital screen-magnification tools to access the curriculum.

Present Level: Rate of Progress - Rahul Verma is currently functioning at grade level with a stable and consistent trajectory of progress, demonstrating the capability to keep pace with Grade 9 curricular expectations when provided with appropriate assistive technology and accessible materials.",
  "social_development": "Present Level: Relationships with Peers and Adults - Rahul maintains warm, respectful, and collaborative relationships with teachers and peers. He contributes enthusiastically to classroom discussions, group projects, and oral question-and-answer sessions.

Present Level: Self-Concept - Rahul exhibits a positive self-identity and high motivation toward academic success, especially in STEM fields. However, he experiences performance-related anxiety concerning high-stakes secondary board examination procedures and future higher education admissions.

Present Level: Social Adjustment - Rahul demonstrates mature social adjustment, navigating the secondary school environment confidently and seeking help appropriately when print access barriers arise.

Present Level: Behaviours That May Impede Learning - No disruptive or maladaptive behaviours are observed; learning is impeded only by ocular fatigue and secondary situational stress during prolonged unadapted visual tasks.",
  "physical_development": "Rahul presents with moderate visual impairment affecting visual acuity for standard printed text (10-12 point) and distant visual stimuli such as the blackboard. His gross and fine motor skills are well developed and age-appropriate. He independently navigates school corridors, classrooms, and common areas without requiring mobility cane assistance. His general health, physical stamina, and energy are normal; however, prolonged visual near-point tasks without optical or digital magnification induce eye strain and fatigue. Environmental considerations such as glare-free illumination, front-row positioning, and frequent visual rest intervals are essential to maintain his physical well-being throughout the school day.",
  "management_needs": "Rahul requires a moderate level of environmental and material management. Environmental modifications include front-row central seating directly aligned with the blackboard to reduce viewing distance, adjustable glare-free ambient lighting, and adequate desk space to accommodate electronic magnification devices and enlarged textbooks. Material resources include large-print textbooks and worksheets printed in 18-24 point font, digital versions of study materials, screen-magnification software, electronic video magnifiers (CCTV), and text-to-speech tools. Human resources include bi-weekly consultative support from a qualified special educator, periodic sessions with the school counsellor for anxiety reduction and transition planning, and regular teacher coordination.",
  "long_term_outcomes": "Rahul aims to complete senior secondary schooling with high academic standing and gain admission into a competitive undergraduate degree program in Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics (STEM). He aspires to pursue professional employment in scientific research or computer technology, taking full advantage of statutory provisions under Section 32 of the RPwD Act 2016, which mandates a five percent reservation and a five-year upper age relaxation in higher educational institutions. His long-term community living outcome is to function as a fully independent adult who utilizes digital assistive technology, self-advocacy skills, and public accommodations to access higher education campuses, professional workplaces, and civic life.",
  "annual_goals": "Annual Goal: Rahul will independently configure and utilize screen-magnification and text-to-speech assistive technology tools to access 100% of his digital Grade 9 curriculum texts and study materials across all subjects.
Short-term Objectives:
1. By the end of Term 1, Rahul Verma will independently open, navigate, and adjust zoom levels on screen-magnification software to read digital textbook chapters with 90% accuracy in tool manipulation across 4 out of 5 observed classroom sessions as measured by teacher observation and student digital logs.
2. By the end of Term 2, Rahul Verma will use screen-magnification combined with text-to-speech software to complete assigned subject readings within standard study periods with 85% task completion across 5 consecutive checks as measured by homework submissions and digital activity logs.
3. By the end of Term 3, Rahul Verma will independently access, read, and highlight key concepts in digital study materials for all subjects using integrated assistive software with 95% proficiency across all academic units as measured by quarterly special education review checklists.
Evaluation Procedures: Teacher observation checklists, student digital access logs, special educator evaluation rubrics
Evaluation Schedule: Quarterly

Annual Goal: Rahul will complete all Grade 9 mathematics and science written assessments using large-print materials and allocated compensatory time, achieving a minimum score of 75%.
Short-term Objectives:
1. By the end of Term 1, Rahul Verma will complete all formative mathematics and science quizzes printed in 18-24 point font within the extended time allowance, obtaining at least 70% marks as measured by teacher-graded assessment records.
2. By the end of Term 2, Rahul Verma will solve multi-step mathematical problems and science diagram-based questions on large-print papers within the extended time limit, achieving at least 75% marks across 4 consecutive classroom tests as measured by test rubrics and work samples.
3. By the end of Term 3, Rahul Verma will complete full-length term examinations in mathematics and science using 18-24 point print and 20 minutes per hour compensatory time, scoring at least 78% as measured by terminal examination results.
Evaluation Procedures: Graded examination papers, timed assessment observation logs, academic grade sheets
Evaluation Schedule: Quarterly

Annual Goal: Rahul will demonstrate self-advocacy and transition planning competency by identifying, requesting, and practicing all eligible secondary board exam accommodations with 100% accuracy during simulated testing conditions.
Short-term Objectives:
1. By the end of Term 1, Rahul Verma will verbally articulate all statutory accommodations available to him under board guidelines and Section 32 of the RPwD Act 2016 with 100% accuracy across 3 counselling sessions as measured by counsellor interview records.
2. By the end of Term 2, Rahul Verma will independently communicate his testing accommodation needs (large print, compensatory time, quiet environment) to all subject teachers prior to scheduled exams in 4 out of 4 instances as measured by teacher confirmation logs.
3. By the end of Term 3, Rahul Verma will complete two full-length simulated board examination papers under formal accommodation protocols (quiet room, 20 minutes extra time per hour, CCTV/magnifier) achieving 100% compliance with examination self-advocacy procedures as measured by mock test coordinator reports.
Evaluation Procedures: Counsellor structured interviews, teacher verification checklists, mock examination documentation
Evaluation Schedule: Quarterly",
  "special_education_services": "A. Special education programs: Rahul will receive specialized instruction delivered by a trained special educator for two sessions per week (45 minutes per session) focusing on assistive technology training, tactile/visual efficiency strategies, and academic adaptation. Counselling and social-emotional support will be provided by the school counsellor for one session per fortnight (40 minutes per session) to address examination-related anxiety and guide transition planning. All special education and related services commence on 2 November 2026 and continue through 31 March 2027.

B. Extended school year services: No, extended school year services are not required as Rahul maintains grade-level academic standing and shows no evidence of substantial regression over routine school breaks.

C. Supplementary aids and modifications: Rahul requires the provision of large-print textbooks (18-24 point font) and accessible learning materials as mandated by NCTE/NCERT Guidelines p.30. Preferential front-row seating centrally aligned with the blackboard will be provided to minimize visual strain. Classroom teachers will provide glare-free, optimized lighting at Rahul's desk and permit visual rest breaks of 3 to 5 minutes during extended reading periods.

D. Assistive technology devices/services: Assistive technology access including screen-magnification software (such as ZoomText or built-in system magnifiers), desktop or portable electronic video magnifiers (CCTV), and text-to-speech tools will be provided as per Section 31 of the RPwD Act 2016 and NCTE/NCERT Guidelines p.30. Rahul will have daily access to these tools in the classroom and library, along with technical support from the special educator.

E. Program modifications for school personnel: Subject teachers will receive orientation and guidance from the special educator on Universal Design for Learning (UDL) principles, digital sharing of teaching notes in advance, accessible document formatting (high contrast, 18-24 pt font), and verbal descriptions of blackboard content as specified in NCTE/NCERT Guidelines p.30.

F. Individual testing modifications: Rahul will receive compensatory extra time of 20 minutes per hour (minimum 25% extended time) on all formative, summative, and formal assessments. He will be provided a separate, quiet testing environment with glare-free illumination to enhance focus and reduce fatigue. Assessment papers will be produced in 18-24 point font, with the permitted use of electronic magnifiers and an option for a qualified scribe or reader during examinations per RPwD Act guidelines and NCTE/NCERT flexible assessment standards (NCTE/NCERT Guidelines p.30). Furthermore, a formulated transition plan with specific targets for board exam preparation and higher education transition guidance is established pursuant to NCTE/NCERT Guidelines p.32 and Section 32 of the RPwD Act 2016.",
  "general_education_participation": "Rahul will participate fully (100% of the school day) in general education academic classrooms, non-academic activities, and school-wide extracurricular events alongside his non-disabled peers. His participation will be supported by accessible large-print materials, digital devices, and specialized instructional adaptations. He will fully engage in physical education and school sports, with modified non-contact activities and orientation to playing areas to prevent collision risks.

Regarding curricular requirements, no second-language exemption is sought or granted. Rahul will participate fully in all prescribed languages and core subjects, accessing literary texts and examinations through enlarged print (18-24 pt), audio aids, and digital magnification tools.",
  "participating_agencies": "1. District Disability Rehabilitation Centre (DDRC), Pune - for assistive technology consultation, clinical low-vision assessments, and technical equipment recommendations.
2. National Institute for the Empowerment of Persons with Visual Disabilities (NIEPVD) Regional Resource Centre - for obtaining large-print supplementary texts, accessible digital books, and specialized educational material support.
3. Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti (NVS) Regional Office, Pune - for administrative approval, allocation of institutional assistive technology, and formal authorization of school-based board exam modifications.
4. District Employment and Career Guidance Cell - for providing higher education and vocational counseling regarding reservation and admission procedures pursuant to Section 32 of the RPwD Act 2016.",
  "coordinated_activities": "1. Instruction: Regular secondary academic instruction in the general classroom enriched with large-print (18-24 point) textbooks, digital soft copies, and screen-magnification tools pursuant to NCTE/NCERT Guidelines p.30, reinforced by bi-weekly specialized instruction.
2. Related Services: Fortnightly school-based psychological counselling to build stress-management strategies and alleviate testing anxiety, combined with low-vision specialist consultations as needed.
3. Employment/Post-secondary Education: Transition planning, college entrance exam orientation, and structured career guidance pursuant to NCTE/NCERT Guidelines p.32 and Section 32 of the RPwD Act 2016, informing Rahul of rights and academic quotas in STEM higher education.
4. Community Experience: Practice in navigating campus libraries, computer laboratories, and local public transit networks independently using low-vision aids and auditory smartphone applications.
5. Activities of Daily Living: Instruction in self-advocacy techniques, maintaining and adjusting personal low-vision hardware/software, and managing ocular health routines during daily study schedules.
6. Functional Vocational Assessment: N/A at age 14 (developmentally appropriate career interest inventories will be administered during Grade 10).",
  "graduation_info": "Certificate Sought: Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) Secondary School Certificate (Class 10) in 2028, followed by Senior School Certificate (Class 12) in 2030.
Expected Year of School Completion: March 2030.
Board Examination Provisions: Rahul is eligible for mandatory board examination accommodations including compensatory extra time (20 minutes per hour), a separate quiet testing room, question papers formatted in 18-24 point font, the use of a desktop or portable electronic video magnifier (CCTV), screen-magnification software, and the option of a reader or scribe. Consistent with Section 6, no second-language exemption is sought or granted; Rahul will appear for all standard language examinations using authorized accessible formats.",
  "recommendations_summary": "Disability Classification: Visual Impairment (moderate low vision) as scheduled under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act 2016. Rahul is entitled to free education in an appropriate environment up to 18 years of age under Section 31 of the RPwD Act 2016.
Recommended Placement: Full inclusion in the Grade 9 general education classroom at Navodaya Vidyalaya, Pune, supported by supplementary aids, assistive technology devices, and itinerant special education services.
Extended School Year Services: Not recommended, as the student exhibits solid academic mastery without regression.
Transportation Needs: Standard school transportation; no specialized transport equipment is required, though peer-escort support during boarding and deboarding is maintained for campus safety.
Annual Review: The next comprehensive annual IEP review will convene on 19 October 2027.",
  "progress_reporting": "Rahul's parents will receive formal written progress reports quarterly, following the same schedule and frequency as reports provided to parents of non-disabled peers at Navodaya Vidyalaya, Pune. Progress on each specific annual goal and short-term objective will be evaluated against objective criteria, including percentage accuracy, teacher observation logs, digital utilization checklists, and completed assessment scores. Special education progress reports will accompany regular term report cards at the end of Term 1, Term 2, and Term 3. In addition to written reports, formal parent-teacher conferences will be conducted at the conclusion of each academic term, with an interim meeting scheduled upon teacher or parent request, culminating in the annual IEP review on 19 October 2027."
}
